title: Dynamics of Majorana tetron qubits under quasiparticle poisoning
abstract: We study the dissipative dynamics of a Majorana tetron qubit in the presence of extrinsic quasiparticle poisoning due to the coupling to external leads. From the Bloch-Redfield equation describing a finite-size topological superconductor hosting four Majorana zero modes, we recover analytical expressions for the steady state, the parity leakage rate, and the decoherence rate of a Majorana qubit at arbitrary values of the charging energy. The analysis shows that the exponential suppression of the dephasing rate is gradually removed by the energy splitting of the qubit states. These results can be useful to understand time-domain experimental data in Majorana qubit prototypes.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes how Majorana tetron qubits lose quantum information due to coupling with external quasiparticles. Using the Bloch-Redfield equation, the authors derive key rates for decoherence and parity leakage. The results are crucial for understanding and improving the time-domain measurements of Majorana qubits in quantum computing prototypes.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dissipative dynamics of a Majorana tetron qubit when subjected to environmental noise from quasiparticle poisoning.
main_result: The analysis yields analytical expressions for the steady state, parity leakage, and decoherence rates, showing how the dephasing rate's exponential suppression is gradually removed by the qubit's energy splitting.
method: The study employs the Bloch-Redfield equation, derived using the Born-Markov approximation, to model the open quantum system dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a Majorana tetron qubit, modeled as a superconducting island hosting four Majorana zero modes, coupled to external leads (the bath). The dynamics are governed by a master equation derived from the total Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Steady state, parity leakage rate, and decoherence rate of the Majorana qubit.
important_parameters: Charging energy (U), direct couplings ($\epsilon$), and coupling strength ($\Gamma_0$). Key regimes include the degenerate ($\epsilon \ll \Gamma_0$) and secular ($\epsilon \gg \Gamma_0$) limits.
main_assumptions: The Born-Markov approximation is used, requiring the bath correlation time to be much shorter than the system evolution time ($	au_D \gg 	au_B$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the tetron island coupled to four fermionic leads, and Figure 2 illustrates the energy-level scheme of the isolated Majorana system.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the full Hamiltonian and the open system dynamics via the Bloch-Redfield equation, deriving the master equation under approximations, and finally analyzing the resulting rates in different energy regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses decoherence mechanisms in solid-state qubits, providing quantitative tools to predict experimental limitations in topological quantum computing platforms.
